source.paraphrase: Do not split a route into a Ruby-on-Rails-style controller. Write the handler on the route so path parameters infer, or build the separated handlers with factory.createHandlers() and spread them. Compose files with app.route().

invariants.why: A handler declared away from the route loses the path-parameter type. Reviewers then see a controller that does not know which route called it.
invariants.fixHint: Write the handler inline on app.get or the other verb. When the handlers must live elsewhere, use factory.createHandlers() and app.get('/api', ...handlers). Mount a sub-app with app.route('/books', books).
invariants.avoid: Spreading createHandlers is the allowed split. app.route takes a Hono app, not a controller method. A class not named Controller, or a Controller method that is not typed Context, is not this rule. A Hono value built by a helper that does not textually contain new Hono or createApp is not seen.

source.paraphrase: Hono answers HEAD by running the GET handler and dropping the body, before route matching. app.head and app.on('HEAD') are never called.

invariants.why: A dedicated HEAD handler looks registered and never runs, so its headers and status are not the ones the client receives.
invariants.fixHint: Handle the request in app.get. When HEAD needs a different header, await next() in middleware and branch on c.req.method === 'HEAD'.
invariants.avoid: Quote style does not matter. createApp() is still a Hono app. A string HEAD inside the GET handler is not a HEAD route. A .head call on a value that is not textually Hono is not this rule.
